answer: Sybil resistance comes from requiring each identity to complete a continuous chain of modular squarings, with each result feeding the next; a Wesolowski proof lets verifiers check the completed delay cheaply. An attacker cannot split one chain across GPUs to remove its sequential latency, and creating many clones requires repeated delay work and hardware. The plume of identities may grow, but each must cross the same computational summit before gaining access at the wharf.
